thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: multiple elevated 5xx and latency alerts for Hosted API + several Dedicated pools in eu-west-3. Triggered by external API failures (AWS control-plane) and downstream auth/observability errors. Paging oncall.

sarah (oncall): I'm on it, acknowledging pager. Starting triage.

raj (infra): Seeing control-plane errors from AWS in eu-west-3, API Gateway and IAM calls intermittently returning 5xx/timeouts. Metric spikes: API latency +4x, 5xx rate up ~18% in last 7m.

lin (runtime): Confirmed increased model-init latencies and some token generation 503s for hosted endpoints that hit remote metadata calls. KV cache warmups failing for some Dedicated shards in eu-west-3.

carla (support): Live customer reports coming in — two enterprise tenants in EU reporting request failures and timeouts. Not yet escalated to account execs.

megan (pm): Customer-impact classification? This looks regional but affects both Hosted and Dedicated. Propose SEV2 for impacted customers and SEV3 for global.

raj (infra): Agreed. Root cause seems to be AWS control-plane API throttling + downstream auth provider (third-party identity) is throwing retries because STS AssumeRole calls are delayed. We also see observability ingestion (3rdparty) failing which hides some traces.

lin (runtime): Immediate mitigations I can do: 1) switch routing policy for eu-west-3 traffic to fallback region (eu-west-1) for new requests; 2) pin dedicated pools to local model caches to avoid control-plane calls; 3) enable degraded-mode DAG that bypasses observability writes. Need greenlight for automated routing change.

sarah (oncall): Give the greenlight for routing fallback and degraded-mode observability off. Prioritize avoiding customer-request failures over metric fidelity.

ops-bot: Routing policy update queued: shift 60% of new requests from eu-west-3 -> eu-west-1. Rolling change in 2 mins.

lin (runtime): Applying pinning to Dedicated shards now — will force local credentials & cached kernels. Running small canary.

raj (infra): Opening SR with AWS: SR# 9876543210. AWS status (console): "Increased error rates for control plane in eu-west-3". Also opening with auth provider (SR# 24680) — they report elevated latency on token exchange.

carla (support): Updating status page draft: "We are investigating elevated errors and latency in our eu-west-3 region impacting API responses. We are routing new traffic to a healthy region and mitigating impact for Dedicated pools. Customers may see intermittent failures; we're working actively." Anyone object?

megan (pm): Post message now and tag impacted customers via support channel. Also start a short customer update template for account teams.

carla (support): Posted status page and emailed affected customers list.

lin (runtime): Canary looks good — fallback routing reduced 5xx rate on canary from 12% -> 1.8%. Rolling to 60% as planned.

sarah (oncall): Good. Keep monitoring. What's the plan for Dedicated capacity that still sits in eu-west-3?

raj (infra): For Dedicated pools: we're temporarily enabling cross-region ingress for control plane operations where feasible, and coordinating with Dedicated-owner teams to gracefully failover overloaded shards. Full migration requires customer consent for data locality — so we'll try pinning + retry-resilience first.

lin (runtime): Patching runtime to short-circuit STS calls with cached tokens for 10m TTL for heavy request paths. Deploying now.

incident-bot: Deploy of cached-token patch succeeded on 6 nodes in eu-west-3.

carla (support): Received confirmation from 3rd party auth — they are seeing a partial outage and are investigating. They provided SR update: "latency spike correlates with elevated regional routing issues; mitigation in progress."

megan (pm): Customer impact: 27 enterprise customers had >3% error rate; 3 customers had >20% errors and we've offered priority handling. Prepare credits/adjustments post-incident.

raj (infra): Observability vendor acknowledged high ingestion latency; we've enabled degraded-mode to avoid blocking request paths (dropped metrics for ~5m window).

lin (runtime): After mitigations, overall 5xx decreased to baseline in eu-west-3 for hosted endpoints that were routed away. Some Dedicated shards are still showing transient errors but trending down.

sarah (oncall): That matches what I see. Keeping pager open for 2h to monitor dependencies and confirm AWS stabilizes.

carla (support): Ongoing comms: Sending tailored update to top 3 impacted customers, CC'ing account teams.

incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff scheduled in 45m. Next oncall is raj.

megan (pm): Action items tracked: 1) Postmortem owner (megan) 2) SR #9876543210 (AWS) and #24680 (auth) to be copied into PIR 3) Customer credits assessment 4) Improve token caching/STS retry backoff 5) Review routing fallback automation.

raj (infra): I'll take handoff. Logging current state and mitigations in the incident doc.

lin (runtime): Adding runtime logs snippet for troubleshooting to the incident doc: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"model":"gpt-3x"}'
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\nDate: ...\nx-request-id: req_abc123\n```

sarah (oncall): Thanks team. If AWS publishes a region-clear we can start shifting requests back gradually and re-enable observability writes. For now leave fallback and cached tokens in place until we see sustained stability for 30m.

ops-bot: Status update: routing fallback at 60% -> 0.5% 5xx cluster-wide; dedicated shard error rate down from 22% -> 6% after pinning.

carla (support): Closing loop for support — sent final interim update to impacted customers: next update in 1h or sooner.

incident-bot: Incident classified SEV2 (regional outage impacting multiple customers). Oncall handoff to raj (infra) at 1865434500. Postmortem owner: megan.

megan (pm): After-action: schedule PIR in 48h, include AWS/auth/observability vendor timelines and gaps. Also prioritize automation to detect 3rd-party control-plane degradations and auto-fallback.

raj (infra): Taking over. Leaving this thread; will update with SR closures and timeline. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
